docs.title: Transformo MCP Server
docs.description: Transformo Labs' own MCP server for the BI team's released Transformo project: the SQL models that turn raw data in the ColumnDB analytics database into the report tables ReportStudio reads. It lists the models and sources, explains a model's columns, tests, and lineage, compiles a model into its SQL, runs read-only queries, and searches Transformo's documentation. Everyone with access to MCP Toolbox can use it: pair the two to query any ColumnDB table, and add the ReportStudio MCP Server to ask the reports built on these models.

docs.title: PingMe MCP Server
docs.description: An MCP server built in-house for PingMe: from every client on this map it reads and searches your chats and messages with their replies, reactions, and members, reads the photos, documents, and voice messages they carry, sends messages, files, and polls, and schedules, edits, forwards, pins, deletes, and reacts to messages. Sign in with Suite Co once, then link each PingMe account by scanning a QR code with your phone, or a bot by its token from @BotMaster; every call runs under one of your own linked accounts, which you add, rename, unlink, or make the default on the account page. A bot picks up what arrived for it since its last check and can put link buttons under the messages and files it sends, but it cannot list chats, browse or search history, open reply threads, see who reacted, or schedule: those need a personal account.

docs.content: An MCP server built in-house for PingMe: from every client on this map it reads and searches your chats and messages with their replies, reactions, and members, reads the photos, documents, and voice messages they carry, sends messages, files, and polls, and schedules, edits, forwards, pins, deletes, and reacts to messages. Sign in with Suite Co once, then link each PingMe account by scanning a QR code with your phone, or a bot by its token from @BotMaster; every call runs under one of your own linked accounts, which you add, rename, unlink, or make the default on the account page. A bot picks up what arrived for it since its last check and can put link buttons under the messages and files it sends, but it cannot list chats, browse or search history, open reply threads, see who reacted, or schedule: those need a personal account. Your own rights: it reads and writes PingMe as your own accounts and bots, keeps no copy of your messages, and every secret it stores is encrypted. You choose which chats assistants may use in the Chat access for assistants section of the account page: every chat except the ones you block, or only the ones you allow, picked one by one or as whole PingMe folders, which follow your edits in PingMe. One choice covers all your linked accounts and bots, for reading, searching, and sending alike; every chat stays open until you save one, and no assistant can change it. Each personal account's link shows up in your PingMe Settings as a device, next to your phone and desktop; log it out from any device where you are signed in and it stops working on the next call, and a bot's link ends when you revoke its token at @BotMaster. Reading voice and round video messages as text goes through Nova Labs and is on request: agree it with your management first, then message Ivan Petrov: t.me/nordline_staff1.

docs.title: Lyra Code Sentinel
docs.description: An AI agent that watches Lyra AI's status page and, when an incident reaches Lyra Code, posts it to the Lyra Code + AI Insights group in PingMe: the issue, the fix under way, and the all-clear, in one thread. Each post keeps Lyra AI's own report apart from what the Lyra Code Gateway saw on its side. It runs as an agent in Nova Chat and stays silent overnight, from 21:00 to 06:00 local time.

docs.title: Metrics MCP Server
docs.description: Next, as an experiment: an MCP server built in-house with one ready-made answer per engineering delivery metric, from CodeVault first and TaskHub later, by team and project, with charts where the client can draw them. It checks whether ready-made metrics answer faster and more consistently than working the numbers out through the connectors, and whether it opens depends on what the experiment shows. Already in development, and planned to run behind the MCP Gateway.
